name: Colosseum
overview: The Colosseum, also known as the Flavian Amphitheatre, is an iconic symbol of Imperial Rome and one of the New Seven Wonders of the World. This massive stone amphitheatre was the largest ever built and could hold up to 80,000 spectators.
history: Built between 70-80 AD under Emperor Vespasian and completed under Emperor Titus, this architectural marvel could hold 50,000-80,000 spectators who watched gladiatorial combats, animal hunts, and even mock naval battles (naumachiae). The arena floor was covered with sand to absorb blood, and a complex system of underground chambers housed gladiators, animals, and stage machinery. Christians were martyred here, and it became a symbol of Imperial Rome's power. After the fall of Rome, it served as housing, workshops, a fortress, and even a Christian shrine. The phrase 'While the Colosseum stands, Rome shall stand; when the Colosseum falls, Rome shall fall; when Rome falls, the world shall fall' reflects its enduring significance as the eternal symbol of Rome.
highlights: Arena floor where gladiatorial battles took place
Multiple levels of seating arranged by social class
Advanced drainage and crowd control systems
tips: Book combined tickets for Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Palatine Hill. Underground and upper tier tours offer unique perspectives. Visit during golden hour for spectacular photos.
